summary: Gyoshu Chujo is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Minobusan University (attested 1996 and 2001).
Gyu Eon Jang works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a professorship at Peking University and was an HK research professor at Geumgang University (attested 2015).

Gyurme Dorje (1950–2020) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Edinburgh and SOAS, completing a PhD under Philip Denwood, alongside traditional teachers. He later served as a research fellow at SOAS (~1988–1998).

György Hazai (1932–2016) was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1949–1954) and held a post at the German Academy of Sciences at Berlin (~1963–1982).
György Kara (1935–2022) specialized in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at Eötvös Loránd University (~1953–1958), he held a post at Indiana University (~1993–2022).

Gérard Colas (born 1952) is an Indologist. He has served as a directeur de recherche and Senior Fellow at CNRS (attested 2004, 2009) and at École des hautes études en sciences sociales (attested 2012).

Gérard Fussman (1940–2022) studied at École Normale Supérieure (~1960–1964) and worked in Indology, history and archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He succeeded Jean Filliozat and served as a professor at the Collège de France (~1984–2011).

Géza Bethlenfalvy (1936–2021) specialized in Tibetology, Indology, and Central Asian studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University under Louis Ligeti, later holding posts there, at the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, the University of Delhi, and the University of Vienna.

Gösta Liebert (1916–1998) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Hjalmar Frisk, Nils M. Holmer, and Stig Wikander (~1945–1950) and held a post at the University of Gothenburg (~1951–1982).

Götz von Selle (1893–1956) was a historian. He studied at the Humboldt University of Berlin, the University of Kiel, and the University of Göttingen, where he later held a post from around 1929 to 1938.

Günter Grönbold (born 1943) is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the Bavarian State Library from around 1974 to 2008, including serving as Head of the South Asia Department (~1976–2008).

Günter Schweiger (born 1941) specialized in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Vienna University of Economics and Business under Gert Klingenschmitt and held a post there from around 1974 to 2009.

H. G. Narahari is an Indologist who studied at the University of Mysore and the University of Madras, where he completed an MA under C. Kunhan Raja. He held posts at Madras and the Adyar Library and Research Centre (attested 1944).
H. V. Nagaraja Rao is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He held posts at the Oriental Research Institute, Mysore, and as a professor at the University of Mysore (attested 2012).
Hachiro Hasebe (born 1950) is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Keio University (~1969–1973) and served as an associate professor at Komazawa University (~1993–2000).
Haeju Sunim is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a visiting lecturer at Harvard University (1996–1997) and as an associate professor of Buddhist studies at Dongguk University (attested 1999).

Haiyan Hu-von Hinüber is an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and sinologist. She studied at Peking University under Kemu Jin and Zhongxin Jiang, later holding posts at the University of Vienna and the University of Freiburg.

Hajime Kitamura (1923–2003) was a linguist and Tibetologist who studied at the University of Tokyo under Tokan Tada. He held posts at NINJAL, the Toyo Bunko, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, Reitaku University, and the Centre for East Asian Cultural Studies.

Hajime Nakamura (1912–1999) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo. He served as a professor at Tokyo, a visiting professor at Stanford, and director of the Eastern Institute and Toho Gakuin.

Hajime Okayama (1948–2022) worked in Buddhist studies, sinology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo and under Xianlin Ji, and held posts at Chūō Bukkyō Gakuin and the University of Tokyo (attested 1988–2013).
